review.authorization: Active integration goal and standing autonomous screening-proxy approval, with all scientific limitations recorded for review.
review.basis: Derived pre-delivery historical Swiss producer portfolio; preserve relative native producer weights and complete protected producer inventories.
limitations: The native Swiss exergy-allocated delivered district-heat mix supplies eight plant-heat contributions totalling 1.10978 MJ per delivered MJ and a separate one-MJ network service. This derived resource represents one MJ at plant: retain the relative producer contributions, divide their coefficients by the nominal total 1.10978 and leave network service and the delivered-heat loss boundary outside this pre-delivery reference. Standard Premise delivery adds its separately reviewed network model once; its loss convention can differ from the historical Swiss delivered mix.

This globally applied historical Swiss generation portfolio is a screening proxy for unspecified heat or missing IAM supply detail, including building residual heat. It includes natural gas, CHP, heat pumps, oil, wood, nuclear and native zero-allocated waste heat. It is not a known future regional portfolio, a reconstruction of non-gas residual fuels, or a measured small-boiler mix. Heat grade, end-use technology, geography, allocation, vintage and score differences remain explicit and unquantified.

Keep complete native producer inventories under distinct fixed identities, excluding them from heat-market relinking. Preserve their source inputs, emissions, allocation, signed quantities and supported uncertainty. The source weights are scaled by one fixed nominal basis conversion; their marginal uncertainty remains, without asserting correlated, sample-normalized portfolio shares. Preserve the native empty zero-allocated MSWI heat handover without adding incineration burdens or credits. Upstream electricity and fuel backgrounds may still respond to their own normal sector updates.

No known IAM volume is removed, no additional residual energy is invented and no efficiency is inferred from allocated fuel draw. The fallback replaces only unspecified composition. A missing source or changed quantity guard remains an error; this does not authorize substituting a network-only service for heat.

activities.comment:
Full activity name: Heat, mixed chips from forest, at furnace 1000kW
Inventory for 1 MJ heat from mixed chips, burned in a furnace with a capacity of 1 MW. Annual efficiency is estimated with 85 % (Hu).;
Synonyms: In UVEK2018 enthalten; 
UUID: 4d188886-a3cb-3e45-92e6-8faf661d7a9d
This module provides heat for end uses.
Location: Could be used for central European conditions
Technology: Efficiency of boiler of average technology available on the market
Time period: Time of publications.
Production volume: na
Sampling: <null>
Extrapolations: none
Uncertainty adjustments: none
BAFU mapped export: unsupported biosphere exchanges excluded; see audit/. Local UUIDs and generic activity classification are export conventions. Source: process_4d188886-a3cb-3e45-92e6-8faf661d7a9d.xml
Geography: Location: Could be used for central European conditions
Technology: Technology: Efficiency of boiler of average technology available on the market
Time period: Time period: Time of publications. Fixed complete producer copy for historical composition. The native Swiss exergy-allocated delivered district-heat mix supplies eight plant-heat contributions totalling 1.10978 MJ per delivered MJ and a separate one-MJ network service. This derived resource represents one MJ at plant: retain the relative producer contributions, divide their coefficients by the nominal total 1.10978 and leave network service and the delivered-heat loss boundary outside this pre-delivery reference. Standard Premise delivery adds its separately reviewed network model once; its loss convention can differ from the historical Swiss delivered mix. This globally applied historical Swiss generation portfolio is a screening proxy for unspecified heat or missing IAM supply detail, including building residual heat. It includes natural gas, CHP, heat pumps, oil, wood, nuclear and native zero-allocated waste heat. It is not a known future regional portfolio, a reconstruction of non-gas residual fuels, or a measured small-boiler mix. Heat grade, end-use technology, geography, allocation, vintage and score differences remain explicit and unquantified. Keep complete native producer inventories under distinct fixed identities, excluding them from heat-market relinking. Preserve their source inputs, emissions, allocation, signed quantities and supported uncertainty. The source weights are scaled by one fixed nominal basis conversion; their marginal uncertainty remains, without asserting correlated, sample-normalized portfolio shares. Preserve the native empty zero-allocated MSWI heat handover without adding incineration burdens or credits. Upstream electricity and fuel backgrounds may still respond to their own normal sector updates. No known IAM volume is removed, no additional residual energy is invented and no efficiency is inferred from allocated fuel draw. The fallback replaces only unspecified composition. A missing source or changed quantity guard remains an error; this does not authorize substituting a network-only service for heat.

activities.comment:
Full activity name: Heat from waste, at municipal waste incineration plant
The multioutput-process 'municipal solid waste to municipal incineration' delivers the co-products 'disposal, municipal solid waste, 22.9% water, to municipal incineration' and 'electricity from waste, at municipal waste incineration plant' and 'heat from waste, at municipal waste incineration plant '. Default allocation 100% to disposal function, 0% to energy production. These allocation factors also apply to emissions of waste heat: i.e. neither electricity nor heat from waste at MSWI does contain any waste heat emissions. Inventoried waste contains 21% paper; 8% Mixed cardbord; 15% plastics; 3% laminated materials; 2% laminated packaging, e.g. tetra bricks; 3% combined goods: dipers; 3% glass; 2% textiles; 8% minerals; 9% natural products; 22% compostable material; 2.65% inert metals; 1% volatile metals; 0.0065% batteries; 0.34% electronic goods; . waste composition (wet, in ppm): upper heating value 13.27 MJ/kg; lower heating value 11.74 MJ/kg; H2O 228830; O 257060; H 48250; C 334230; S 1119; N 3123.8; P 893.79; B 7.1933; Cl 6866.2; Br 13.552; F 56.358; I 0.0121; Ag 0.714; As 0.62521; Ba 149.04; Cd 11.748; Co 1.3453; Cr 315.21; Cu 1212.8; Hg 1.4424; Mn 259.36; Mo 1.9551; Ni 107.38; Pb 502.43; Sb 22.564; Se 0.31969; Sn 73.44; V 9.2147; Zn 1311.2; Be n.a.; Sc n.a.; Sr n.a.; Ti n.a.; Tl n.a.; W n.a.; Si 48510; Fe 29996; Ca 14062; Al 12420; K 2059.7; Mg 3377.7; Na 5143.9; Share of carbon in waste that is biogenic 60.4%. Share of iron in waste that is metallic/recyclable 60%. Net energy produced in MSWI: 1.01MJ/kg waste electric energy and 2.16MJ/kg waste electric energy Allocation of energy production: no substitution or expansion. Total burden allocated to waste disposal function of MSWI. One kg of this waste produces 0.1888 kg of slag and 1 kg of residues, which are landfilled. ;; UUID: cc476d2d-20a3-3064-a77e-8d173cc5ac5e
waste-specific air and water emisions from incineration, auxiliary material consumption for flue gas cleaning. Short-term emissions to river water and long-term emisisons to ground water from slag compartment (from bottom slag) and residual material landfill (from solidified fly ashes and scrubber slugde). Process energy demands for MSWI.
Location: Specific to the technology mix encountered in Switzerland in 2000. Well applicable to modern incineration practices in Europe, North America or Japan.
Technology: average Swiss MSWI plants in 2000 with electrostatic precipitator for fly ash (ESP), wet flue gas scrubber and 29.4%,  SNCR 32.2%,  SCR-high dust 24.6%,  SCR-low dust  DeNOx facilities and 13.8% without Denox  (by burnt waste, according to Swiss average). Share of waste incinerated in plants with magnetic scrap separation from slag : 50%. Gross electric efficiency technology mix 12.997% and Gross thermal efficiency technology mix 25.57% 
Time period: Waste composition as given in literature reference, theoretical data or other source. Transfer coefficients for modern Swiss MSWI. Emission speciation based on early 90ies data.
Production volume: na
Sampling: waste-specific calculation based on literature data 
Extrapolations: Typical elemental transfer coefficients from current studies for modern MSWI, completed with data from coal power plants and estimates, adapted for inert/burnable waste.
Uncertainty adjustments: uncertainty of waste input composition data derived from generic formula GSD(c) = N*ln(c)+1
